extraction.name: CoNLL-2003 Shared Task: Language-Independent Named Entity Recognition
extraction.description: The CoNLL-2003 shared task dataset for language-independent named entity recognition, containing English and German news text with annotations for persons, organizations, locations, and miscellaneous entities.
extraction.creator: Erik F. Tjong Kim Sang, Fien De Meulder
extraction.citeAs: Tjong Kim Sang, E. F., & De Meulder, F. (2003). Introduction to the CoNLL-2003 Shared Task: Language-Independent Named Entity Recognition.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The data was collected from news corpora. English data was taken from the Reuters Corpus (news stories between August 1996 and August 1997). German data was taken from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus, specifically articles from the Frankfurter Rundschau newspaper (written in one week at the end of August 1992).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Reuters Corpus (English) and ECI Multilingual Text Corpus / Frankfurter Rundschau (German).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: English: August 1996 to August 1997. German: August 1992.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The raw data underwent linguistic preprocessing including tokenization, part-of-speech tagging, and chunking. For English, the MBT tagger was used. For German, the Treetagger was used for lemmatization, tagging, and chunking.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Preprocessing included tokenization, part-of-speech tagging, and chunking. The data was formatted with one word per line, empty lines for sentence boundaries, and four fields per line: word, POS tag, chunk tag, and named entity tag using the IOB scheme.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Named entity tagging of English and German training, development, and test data was done by hand at the University of Antwerp. Mostly MUC conventions were followed. An extra category 'MISC' was added for miscellaneous entities.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset consists of news articles, which may not represent other genres or languages. The 'MISC' category is described as very diverse. The data is limited to English and German.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation of Named Entity Recognition systems.
